name: Hayman's Sloe Gin
base_ingredient: Hayman's English gin with steeped sloe berries
production: Wild-harvested English sloes steeped in Hayman's gin for 3-4 months (old family recipe)
history: 1863 | Hayman ancestor (a pharmacist) buys a gin rectifying business in Cale Street, Chelsea
1969 | Christopher Hayman joins the family business
expressions: Hayman's Royal Dock Gin | navy strength
serve_official: Sloe gin with lemon/citrus tonic and lemon peel; or Sloe Gin Cooler: 50 ml with bitter lemon in a highball, lemon zest
notes: Botanical list includes the base gin's 10 botanicals plus sloe. Gin Guild suggests using it in place of red wine in venison or duck casseroles.
